posts.title: "Back In The Saddle" by Luke Combs
posts.description: I get that mainstream country-rock productions like this want a fairly forward 2-3kHz region to cut through on small speakers and mobile devices, but I don’t think that means the kick needs to sound quite as gutless as this? I mean, compare it with something like Ella Langley’s 'Choosin' Texas', for instance – not only does that feel weightier on full-range systems, but it also cuts through better on small speakers. ...Read the whole review on on TheMixReview.org !

posts.title: "Iloveitiloveitiloveit" by Bella Kay
posts.description: One of the simplest ways to add energy to a sparse musical texture without obviously adding ’extra instruments’ is to just change the timbre and thickness of the instruments that are already there, and there’s a great example of this idea in action here when the first chorus lands. posts.title: "Movin' To The Sun" by Hugel, Imael Angel & Ultra Naté
posts.description: There are a number of nice little production moves that are worth spotting in this recent EDM hit. The verse-section’s 3/16 lead-vocal delay spins (eg. on the first “sun” at 0:02) are very much stock in trade for this genre, but what I like about them here is the way they’re contrasted against the retriggered quarter-note vocal sample fragments (eg. at 0:10-0:12). Then there’s the canny high-pass filter automation leading into the main chorus/hook entry at 0:32, where the low end of the synths begins progressively falling away from about 0:29, providing a greater contrast (and therefore greater impact) when the chorus’s powerful kick+bass combo finally arrives – something you can see very clearly if you look at a spectrum analyser. ...Read the whole review on on TheMixReview.org !
